newsitem.title: HAITI: Canadian troops to remain in Haiti until year-end.
newsitem.headline: Canadian troops to remain in Haiti until year-end.

text.p: Canadian troops will stay in Haiti through the end of 1997, past the current July 31 deadline for withdrawal of the U.N. peacekeeping mission, Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Wednesday after meeting President Rene Preval.
"The Canadian military will stay here until the end of the month of December," Axworthy told Reuters after leaving the presidential palace.
"The president originally asked (last November) that the U.N. remain in Haiti for 12 months, which indicated to us there is a need for a longer-term stay to guarantee security," he added.
He said the mission would still be carried out under the U.N. umbrella, but the size and composition of the force had not been determined. There are currently about 700 Canadian troops in Haiti.
Preval indicated to Haitian journalists in December that he would not ask for a new extension of the U.N. peacekeeping mission.
Axworthy said that Canadians had committed themselves to development and assistance projects in Haiti for the next five years.
He was scheduled to visit Canadian troops and U.N. Special Representative Enrique Ter Horst after his meeting with Preval.
Haiti has been rocked by a wave of violence over the past month in which as many as 40 people, including up to seven police officers, have been killed.
